synthesis: Lemma 3 first removes Farey coprimality by replacing it with Mobius-weighted unrestricted denominator sums. Bernoulli expansion then expresses centered power moments as finite combinations of the S_{r-1} family, while the Kubert distribution relation makes a full nonodd Kubert sum a nonzero scalar multiple of S_{s-1}; Lemma 2 turns square-root cancellation for each admissible S-index into the zero-free quotient condition zeta(z+s)/zeta(z) equivalent to RH.
source_support: Unit u08 proves the coprimality-removal transform. Unit u09 applies it with power sums and Bernoulli polynomials, obtaining finite S_{r-1} decompositions and the displayed quadratic and cubic S_1 identities. Unit u15 applies the same transform together with Kubert subdivision, and its n=1 specialization gives a full Farey sum proportional to S_{s-1}. Unit u07 computes the Dirichlet series of S_s as zeta(z+s)/zeta(z) and proves the square-root estimate is RH-equivalent in the stated half-plane.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes a combinatorial constraint-removal step with two different representation reductions—Bernoulli triangularization and Kubert distribution—and then identifies their shared analytic denominator as the invariant RH-sensitive signal.
limits: Only the displayed quadratic and cubic moments are shown to isolate S_1 and hence to be RH-equivalent; a generic power moment is merely a finite S-family combination. The regular Kubert criterion requires an extendable parameter, a nonzero nonodd projection, and Re(s)>=3/2 when Lemma 2 is applied to S_{s-1}; the s=1 log-sine case uses a separate modified identity. Formula-level coefficients remain extraction-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because four distinct units establish every link in the transform-to-S-to-Dirichlet-quotient chain; the result is a concrete shared mechanism, not a thematic juxtaposition, and the differing parameter and parity restrictions are preserved.

synthesis: The Kubert functional equation rigidifies K_s into even and odd directions, and the symmetric full Farey transform detects only the nonodd projection by mapping it to a scalar multiple of S_{s-1}. Polylogarithm, Hurwitz-zeta, Bernoulli, and Clausen formulas therefore give different coordinates for that same regular signal, while the singular log-sine and half-interval log-tangent criteria reach Chebyshev prime data through finite products, Mobius inversion, and, for tangent, a dyadic difference.
source_support: Unit u14 states the two-dimensional parity decomposition, the special-function bases, and the conditional extension to R/Z. Units u15 and u16 evaluate the Farey transform and prove that a nonodd f in K_s has full sum zeta(s)(c1+c2)S_{s-1}, then translate this into polylogarithm, Hurwitz-zeta, Bernoulli, and Clausen criteria. Unit u15 separately identifies the modified s=1 log-sine sum with psi(x). Unit u17 derives the half-interval log-tangent sum as one half of psi(x)-psi(x/2), up to its constant, from finite tangent products and the same Mobius removal lemma.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis uses parity to identify the transform's detectable quotient direction, recognizes several special functions as coordinate changes on that direction, and separates that regular basis mechanism from the boundary trigonometric product mechanisms that land in prime-weight rather than S-family formulas.
limits: Odd functions have identically vanishing symmetric full sums and cannot carry the regular criterion. The regular RH equivalence is stated for Re(s)>=3/2 with the listed basis exclusions and extension conditions. Log-sine at s=1 and half-interval log-tangent are not interchangeable members of the regular K_s basis argument: each needs its own finite-product identity, and tangent yields a dyadic Chebyshev difference rather than directly S_{s-1}.
quality_reason: Accepted because u14-u16 jointly prove a basis-independent nonodd projection mechanism, while u15 and u17 concretely explain the related logarithmic trigonometric boundary cases; acceptance is qualified so the distinct special-case proofs are not collapsed into one unsupported identity.

synthesis: Farey rank error is first rewritten in Bernoulli-Mobius coordinates, so its squared discrepancy becomes a sum of pairwise Bernoulli correlations. The generalized Dedekind three-term relation then permits cyclic symmetrization of the resulting triple sum, replacing the three correlation orientations by explicit gcd corrections that cancel down to Franel's exact quadratic identity.
source_support: Unit u18 proves the Farey transform for B_1(a rho)B_1(b rho) and the cyclic three-term relation for the modified generalized Dedekind sums, including pairwise and triple gcd corrections. Unit u19 rewrites each rank error using the earlier Bernoulli-Mobius formula, expands the square, invokes u18 to obtain three cyclic copies of the triple sum, and reduces their gcd terms to the displayed Franel formula.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis reconstructs a dependency that neither unit supplies alone: u18 provides a local reciprocity rule for three Dedekind orientations, and u19 makes global permutation symmetry manufacture exactly those orientations so opaque correlations can be replaced by gcd-weighted arithmetic.
limits: This is an exact structural derivation of Franel's identity, not an independent asymptotic estimate or a proof of RH. The extracted source is formula-dense, so exact signs, coefficients, and gcd factors should be checked against the scan before formal quotation, although the transformation sequence and dependency are clear.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two distinct units are logically complementary: the three-term relation only prepares the reduction, and the discrepancy expansion plus cyclic averaging is required to deploy it. Their combination yields a concrete representation change and cancellation mechanism unavailable from either parent alone.
